title: Cost + Latency Pathfinder dashboard — wires & grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
This note collects early UX thinking, wireframe descriptions, and a groomed backlog for a lightweight first-pass dashboard that helps engineers and SREs trace invocation-level latency and per-token cost back to root causes. Working name: "Pathfinder" — i.e., help customers find the path of cost and latency through an invocation.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers need to understand why specific invocations are expensive or slow at token granularity.
- Existing console views show aggregate per-route cost or per-model latency but lack an invocation timeline + token attribution surface that is quick to navigate.
- Primary users: backend engineers instrumenting clients, platform owners diagnosing regressions after model rollouts, product owners tracking unit economics.

Goals (MVP):
1) Surface a per-invocation timeline that shows token emission times and cumulative cost curve.
2) Provide a token-level breakdown for a selected invocation showing latency contribution, model variant, KV cache hits, and quantization profile.
3) Allow quick histograms / aggregation across many invocations by token position, prompt length, and model variant.
4) Integrate with tracing context (trace id -> invocation) so SREs can pivot to full traces.

User stories (high priority):
- As an SRE, I want to open a single slow invocation and see which tokens and steps introduced the most latency so I can decide whether to roll back a model rollout.
- As an ML infra engineer, I want to filter invocations by model variant and quantization profile so I can compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
- As a product manager, I want to see the 95th and 99th token-level latencies over time for a route to decide on batching/kv-cache thresholds.

Wireframe components (desktop-first):
1) Invocation Timeline (left pane, 35% width)
   - List of invocations with brief meta: route name, model, total tokens, total cost, avg token-latency, status (ok/timeout/fallback).
   - Inline sparklines for token-latency distribution (compact).
   - Search and filter bar at top: time range, route, model, status, trace id.
   - Quick action: "open selected in timeline center"

2) Token Waterfall (center pane, 45% width) — primary investigative area
   - X-axis: token position (1..n). Y-axis shows cumulative latency (stacked bars) or absolute per-token latency.
   - Each token's bar is segmented: model compute, kernel overhead, queue/dispatch, network (if applicable), KV lookup. Colors map to latency sources.
   - Hover over token: tooltip with exact ms, estimated cost cents/token, top contributing kernel, whether KV cache hit and resulting delta.
   - Click token: opens a right-side detail flyout.

3) Token Detail Flyout (right pane, 20% width)
   - Token text (if not PII) or masked preview + tokenizer piece breakdown (byte offsets).
   - Cost attribution: breakdown of cost buckets that generated token (compute-time, memory paging, kernel fallback).
   - Model meta: model id + variant, quantization (int8/4bit), selected kernel, gpu type.
   - Tracing links: link to full trace, logs, and applicable rollout ID.
   - Quick diff: button to compare this invocation to baseline (e.g., previous model version).

Interactions / microcopy notes:
- Default view groups very long invocations (>1024 tokens) into a condensed mode; user can expand.
- Hover interaction latency must be sub-100ms in UI (client-side cached fields).
- For privacy, default token text is masked; allow opt-in to show token strings for orgs with appropriate settings.
- Provide a small legend toggle that explains colors and buckets inline.

Data model & telemetry inputs (MVP minimal set):
- per-invocation: invocation_id, route, model_id, model_variant, start_ts, end_ts, total_tokens, total_cost_estimate
- per-token stream: token_index, token_bytes, delta_ms, compute_ms, queue_ms, kv_hit_boolean, kv_delta_ms, kernel_id, gpu_id, cumulative_ms
- aggregated metrics: 50/95/99 token-latency by route/model, avg cost/token by token position bucket (1-8, 9-64, 65-256, >256)
- trace link mapping: invocation_id -> distributed_trace_id

Queries & sketches (examples to hand to infra):
- Fast read: select token_index, compute_ms, queue_ms, kv_hit from token_stream where invocation_id = :id order by token_index
- Aggregation: group by token_index_bucket, model_variant, compute percentiles for compute_ms; return counts and avg cost/token
- Precompute idea: maintain a small materialized table of per-invocation summary to power the left pane list (keeps timeline fast).

Performance constraints and SLOs for UI queries:
- Drill-in (single invocation token stream) must return < 500ms for invocations up to 2k tokens (cached hot paths).
- Aggregation queries for 24h window across 1m invocations should return progressively: lightweight summary < 2s, heavy percentile surfaces async with a progress indicator.

Privacy & perms:
- Token previews gated by org-level PII policy. Default to masked.
- Only users with tracing or debug role can click-through to raw token text.

Edge cases and fallbacks:
- Missing token timings (partial telemetry): show available buckets and label missing segments.
- Fallbacks to cheaper model: UI should annotate when invocation used a fallback model variant and show delta vs primary model.

Groomed backlog (sorted, with rough estimates):
1) MVP token-waterfall + left-invocation-list (3 weeks, 3 engineers, 2 designer) — acceptance: single-invocation drill < 500ms and flyout with cost breakdown.
2) Aggregation histograms + token-position buckets (1 week) — acceptance: can produce 50/95/99 curves for selected route.
3) Trace integration + trace-id search (1 week) — acceptance: link opens SRE trace viewer with correct context.
4) Privacy toggle & masking controls (0.5 week) — acceptance: token text masked by default, unmask workflow audited.
5) Bulk compare mode (compare two invocations side-by-side) (2 wks) — acceptance: ability to highlight token deltas and cost deltas.
6) Materialized per-invocation summary table (infra work) (2 wks) — acceptance: left-pane list query consistently < 200ms for 1k invocations.
7) Mobile responsive condensed view (1 wk) — low priority.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Engineers can find and open any invocation in the last 7 days and see token-level latency segments.
- Hover shows ms + cents/token for each token, and flyout shows model/quantization metadata.
- Dashboard respects org PII controls and logs unmask events.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we store raw token bytes in telemetry or only metadata (token index + hashed token id)? Security team leaning towards hashed ids + masking by default — need policy signoff.
- Cost model: should we display an estimated cost per token derived from kernel time * cost-per-GPU-second, or a simplified cents/token provided by billing pipeline? Billing prefers the latter for consistency.
- When to precompute vs compute on-demand for long windows. Ops prefers materialized summaries for 24h.

Next steps (for next sync):
- Design: quick InVision/figma wires for center waterfall + flyout (design owner: Sana). Due: 2025-11-20.
- Infra: spike on storing token_stream rows and benchmark a single-invocation read path (owner: Diego). Due: 2025-11-14.
- Security: PII storage policy decision (owner: Aaron). Due: 2025-11-17.
- Product: prepare launch checklist and potential beta customer list (owner: Maya). Due: 2025-11-22.

Notes to self / rough ideas to explore later:
- "Pathfinder mode": automatically detect the token range that contributed 80% of additional latency and center the view there. Could be a helpful default for long outputs.
- "Chargeback lens": show a simulated monthly chargeback per feature (route) by extrapolating from tokens-per-invocation * volume. Useful for conversations with finance.
- Small UX delight: animate cumulative cost curve as tokens render to help eyeball the steep regions. Keep animation short (250ms).

Slack snippets / links for meetings:
- Figma: (tbd)
- Draft PR to console: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/412
- Infra spike ticket: JIRA-REL-7890

End of note.

(Longer-term: if this lands we can iterate on more advanced attribution like kernel-level stack traces, cross-invocation cache warmness maps, and cost-aware rollout suggestions.)
